reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the decision and canonical pair, returned first to the 2026–2027 adopted regulations and faculty programme tables. Recomputed each year, checked assessment, elective limits and progression clauses, and reconsidered the actual course contributions, credit totals, offerings and finished audience fields.
findings: Digital Society is an English full-time three-year BA. The current FASoS regulations and faculty programme table agree on 60 EC in each year. Years one and two contain 21 compulsory components totalling 120 EC, including two 1 EC mentor schemes. Year three requires 30 EC of approved electives, 4 EC of Research Experimentation Zone, 9 EC of Controversies in Digital Society and 17 EC of Bachelor Thesis. The year-three mentor scheme is optional at 0 EC. The 30 EC remain genuine choice space. The regulations allow a 24–30 EC minor, exchange, a 12–24 EC approved internship, a 3–12 EC literature exam and approved electives. An approved mix must cover the full 30 EC. Specified later electives can make up a shortfall. The interest directions and possible minors do not constitute formal pathways of this BA.

Year two normally requires positive binding study advice at 45.5 first-year EC. Year three including study abroad requires all 60 first-year EC. Thesis entry requires those 60 EC and at least 45 EC in year two. Article 7.3 distinguishes negative binding advice below 30 EC and conditional continuation at 30–45 EC. Students request an exception through a study-plan meeting. Module registration also registers the first exam. Active attendance is expected at all meetings, with compulsory meetings and assessed participation governed by the course. The 17 EC thesis takes place in periods 4–6, receives a grade from the supervisor and a second grader, and follows course book deadlines and requirements. The 4 EC Research Experimentation Zone takes place in periods 1–2 and uses the E-P-F scale. The outline establishes credits and component function; specific module content is bounded by the official public sources.

The current sources independently support Virtual Worlds in year one and Critical Making in year two. The optional third-year mentor scheme contributes zero credits. The final 17 EC thesis and 4 EC research experimentation are separate. Course names and the programme description support the stated partial relationships without assuming exact module methods where the public catalogue does not describe them. UCR’s options have substantial shared digital ground in data, algorithms, media and AI ethics. The broad plan adds digital publics, policy reasoning and a limited creative practice component. The technical plan develops systems, neural networks and predictive and decision methods with social context. Public Policy Analysis and Creative Communication Laboratory contribute bounded skills and do not imply a reproduction of specialist digital policy or critical making. Both complete schedules pass the current offering and prerequisite rules.
